components.name: LiteRT-LM

components.name: LiteRT NPU runtime for Google Tensor
components.note: Lets LiteRT-LM use the Tensor G5's TPU (libLiteRtDispatch_GoogleTensor.so). The TPU's own driver is the phone's, not Robot's.

components.name: llama.cpp (with ggml)
components.note: Runs your own GGUF model file on the CPU, in the model process only (librobot_llama.so, built from the tag's source by tools/build_llama.sh): llama.cpp's libllama, ggml with its CPU backend, and its chat-template code. The JSON for Modern C++ it vendors has its own entry.

components.name: KleidiAI
components.copyright: Copyright 2024-2026 Arm Limited and/or its affiliates
components.note: Arm's matrix kernels for the CPU, compiled into Robot's llama.cpp library (librobot_llama.so) at the release llama.cpp b11200 names; ggml picks them at run time.

components.name: LLVM libc++
components.note: The C++ standard library (libc++ and libc++abi), linked statically into Robot's llama.cpp library (librobot_llama.so) and its fast translation engine (librobotmt.so) by the Android NDK. Its text: libc++'s and libc++abi's licences as the NDK states them.

components.name: slimt
components.note: Runs Mozilla's Bergamot translation models: Robot's fast translation engine (librobotmt.so, in the :mt process only), built by tools/build_robotmt.sh from the pinned commit with Robot's own wrapper. GPL-2.0 or later, used here under GPL-3.0; it holds MPL-2.0 code derived from browsermt/bergamot-translator and browsermt/marian-dev and Apache-2.0 code from browsermt/ssplit. Its source: the commit above, which tools/build_robotmt.sh fetches and checks, and Robot's mt/src/main/cpp.

components.name: ruy
components.note: The matrix multiplication library slimt uses, compiled into the fast translation engine (librobotmt.so); it picks its NEON kernels at run time.

components.name: cpuinfo
components.copyright: Copyright (c) 2019 Google LLC; Copyright (c) 2017-2018 Facebook Inc.; Copyright (C) 2012-2017 Georgia Institute of Technology
components.note: Tells ruy what the processor can do; compiled into the fast translation engine (librobotmt.so).

components.name: SentencePiece (in the fast translation engine)
components.note: Splits text into the translation models' word pieces; compiled into the fast translation engine (librobotmt.so). Its text holds the licences of the parts it bundles: protobuf-lite, Abseil and Darts-clone (each its own entry here) and esaxx (MIT), which is only for training models and isn't built into Robot.

components.name: Protocol Buffers lite (in SentencePiece)
components.note: Reads SentencePiece's model files; compiled into the fast translation engine (librobotmt.so).

components.name: Abseil (in SentencePiece)

components.name: Darts-clone (in SentencePiece)
components.note: A compact dictionary SentencePiece's text normalizer uses; compiled into the fast translation engine (librobotmt.so).

components.note: Settings › Conversation › Tell speakers apart: labels a transcript's lines by voice, and your own voice (Your voice). “TitaNet-S” by NVIDIA, under the NeMo toolkit's licence (Apache-2.0), as its model card says. components.name: Wikipedia text

components.name: Brave Search API
components.note: Web search with your own Brave key (0.9): results are used for one answer and never stored; the card says “Powered by Brave” unless you turn that line off (optional in Brave's terms).

components.name: DuckDuckGo Instant Answer API
components.note: Web search's free DuckDuckGo Instant Answers (1.0), when you choose them: short answers only, never a full list of results. The card credits DuckDuckGo (“Results from DuckDuckGo”) and each answer's source with its link, as the API asks; Wikipedia's text keeps its CC BY-SA 4.0 credit. Robot names itself in the API's t parameter (the same for every Robot) and is free and non-commercial.
